content.text:
I added `recordLogin(email, callback)` to `src/services/auth-service.js` in the same callback style as the rest of that file. `npm test` passes all 15 tests.

**How it works:** it finds the active user with that email, sets `last_login_at` to the current time, and calls back with `(null, updatedUser)`. If no active user has that email, including a soft-deleted one, it calls back with `(null, null)` and changes nothing. Errors go to `callback(err)`. The time is stored as an ISO string, the same format as `deleted_at`.

**Two new repository methods:** your first rule means the service can't use `query()` or `update()` directly. `UserRepository` had no way to look a user up by email or update a login time, so I added two methods to `src/repositories/user-repository.js`:
- `findActiveByEmail(email)`
- `recordLogin(id, when)`

Inside, `recordLogin` uses the repository methods and turns their Promise results into the callback.

**Tests:**
- In `tests/auth-service.test.js`: an active user gets a current timestamp, and a soft-deleted user gets `null`.
- In `tests/repositories.test.js`: one test for each of the two new repository methods, as your second rule requires.
